hints.title: Minimum Element Tie-Breaking
hints.text: In each operation, select the minimum value, resolving ties by choosing the smallest index.

hints.title: Priority Tracking
hints.text: Pair each value with its original index so the minimum element and lowest index can be popped immediately.

hints.title: Multiplication Replacement
hints.text: Multiply the extracted minimum value by the multiplier and reinsert it into the heap, repeating k times.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getFinalState(self, nums: list[int], k: int, multiplier: int) -> list[int]:
        import heapq
        # Min-heap of (val, idx)
        pq = [(val, idx) for idx, val in enumerate(nums)]
        heapq.heapify(pq)
        
        for _ in range(k):
            val, idx = heapq.heappop(pq)
            val *= multiplier
            heapq.heappush(pq, (val, idx))
            
        res = [0] * len(nums)
        for val, idx in pq:
            res[idx] = val
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Each multiplication performs a logarithmic extraction and insertion.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear searches per step take O(k * n) which is slower for large k.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Uses min-heap with index tie-breaking to maintain smallest elements.
